category_title: Students who use overprotectiveness and aggression to control partners
scenario_title: Reflective interview on relationship triggers and controlling behavior
minimal_context: The student is participating in a one-on-one interview session with a researcher to discuss relationship behaviors.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Welcome to our first interview session. Today we are going to reflect on your relationship behaviors and how you handle situations with your partner.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I feel [deep sigh] it's not my place; I feel overprotective sometimes. The problem is she doesn't like males touching her, so I feel it's my responsibility to sort out the problems that she's having.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Can you explain what that means for you?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: [Shuffling in chair] Because if I don't do it nothing will get done [pause] the problem keeps going on and on and on. I like to protect my girlfriend (pause) which I have been controlling, sir. It makes me feel as though she needs me, sir. Like I'm wanted.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What happens when you see her interacting with other guys, for example, if you think she is flirting?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: She gives them a special look that she only gives to me! At my previous school, my partners always cheated on me. I snap and lose control... You know, get mad, get angry, usually go outside and bang doors.
